name: Executive order of August 4, 1882 restoring to the public domain the reserve set apart for the Muache, Capote and Weeminuche Utes on February 7, 1879
promises: Royce records that a reservation promised to these bands under the agreement of November 9, 1878 was set apart by executive order of February 7, 1879.
Royce records that Congress never ratified that agreement and that it was superseded by the agreement of March 6, 1880, ratified with amendments on June 15, 1880.
today: Under the Act of June 15, 1880 (21 Stat. 199) and the Act of July 28, 1882 (22 Stat. 178), a reservation about 110 miles long and 15 miles wide was surveyed for the Southern Utes inside their 1868 reservation (ICC findings, Docket 328, 1966).

openQuestions: The scanned Royce schedule is jumbled; whether the bands ever occupied the 1879 reserve was not settled.
This order revoked an executive-order reserve tied to an agreement Congress superseded; no court, Commission or government finding about this land and this order was located.
The Southern Ute and Ute Mountain Ute accounts of the 1879 reserve were not located.

Audit 2026-11-08: Royce's row for the February 7, 1879 order says it was made 'in compliance with agreement of Nov. 9, 1878'; that date added to the first promise. No finding about the 1878 agreement's reserve was located, so under the project rules this stays 'no breach found yet'.

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for Ute, Confederated Bands of Ute, Ute executive order 1879, Ute August 4 1882; 100 Ct. Cl. 413 (1943) only lists the February 7, 1879 order among additions to the reservation, and the 1946 to 1947 Ute addition case concerned the 1875 order only; nothing new on this reserve.
